stem: What is the sum of all solutions to the equation \(\sqrt{2x + 3} - \sqrt{x + 1} = 1\)?
solution: Isolate one radical: \(\sqrt{2x + 3} = 1 + \sqrt{x + 1}\). Square both sides: \(2x + 3 = 1 + 2\sqrt{x + 1} + x + 1\).
Check both in the original equation: \(\sqrt{1} - \sqrt{0} = 1\) and \(\sqrt{9} - \sqrt{4} = 1\). Both are solutions, so the sum is \(-1 + 3 = 2\).
(Dividing both sides of \(x + 1 = 2\sqrt{x + 1}\) by \(\sqrt{x + 1}\) would lose the solution \(x = -1\).)
verify:
x = symbols('x', real=True)
cands = solve(Eq((x + 1)**2, 4*(x + 1)), x)
sols = [c for c in cands if sqrt(2*c + 3) - sqrt(c + 1) == 1]
assert sorted(sols) == [-1, 3]
assert [Rational(a) for a in spr_answers] == [sum(sols)]
